sources.entry: Cyrus IMAP - Email (IMAP/POP3), contacts and calendar server. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause-Attribution C

summary.one_liner: Cyrus IMAP is an open source mail server (developer version 3.13 in this README) that serves email over IMAP, POP3, JMAP, CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Cyrus as an IMAP server intended to run on "sealed" servers where normal users do not log in; the mailbox database is kept in a private part of the filesystem and users access content through JMAP, IMAP, POP3, CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV. It says multiple concurrent read/write connections to the same mailbox are permitted, and that it supports access control lists on mailboxes and storage quotas on mailbox hierarchies. Optional Xapian-based search is mentioned in the build notes. The README covers building from release tarballs (./configure, make, make install), from git (autoreconf first), and building a set of dependencies via a cyruslibs build.sh script. Upgrade notes and developer docs are referenced in the repository.
use_cases: serve IMAP and POP3 mailboxes to clients
how_to_run: ./build.sh (optional: build cyruslibs dependencies, git source for version 3.0 or later)
notable: Designed for sealed servers: users never log in to the host; all access is via mail and DAV protocols
Supports JMAP, IMAP, POP3, CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV in one server
Concurrent read/write access to the same mailbox, with ACLs and quotas on mailbox hierarchies
Stable 3.12 series still receives security fixes while 3.13 is in development
caveats: Developer version 3.13 is under active development and not considered stable; the README points to 3.12 for stable use
Building from git needs many more dependencies; the README recommends building the cyruslibs dependencies first
OS distribution packages are not maintained by the Cyrus team and may be out of date
